layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: the at-large congressional district, the whole state

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; one feature, measured 2026-11-12: Wyoming elects one representative from the whole state, so the one district is the state, which TIGER names "Congressional District (at Large)" (CD120 "00") and the card prints by that name. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same district, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 23 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 23 features, measured 2026-11-12. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Wyoming county is governed by an elected board of county commissioners, and also elects officers such as a clerk, a treasurer, an assessor, a sheriff and a county attorney. No list of them was read in this pass, so the card says how the county is governed and names nobody. Recorded as gap wy-county-officials.

layers.label: Wyoming Senate District
layers.rank_note: 31 Senate districts, each electing one senator

source.answers: The Senate district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 31 features, measured 2026-11-12, which differs from the 2024 vintage (layer 5) only by slivers in two districts (intersection-over-union 0.99682 or more, measured that day). Wyoming draws two House districts mostly inside each Senate district, but the pairs match only to within 0.89 of each other by area, so each map is simplified on its own. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wy-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Legislature's own member feed (wyoleg.gov, the data its member pages read, for the calendar year of the run): each senator's name, party, e-mail address at wyoleg.gov, the one telephone the feed prints, unlabelled, and page. The feed's address, birth and family fields are never read.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 47 unified districts, about 5,250 km2 of land on average, plus the Census's placeholder for ground in no school district, drawn from a mirrored tile archive; with the 1 elementary district they cover the state's land

source.answers: The unified school district covering the point, which runs every grade for it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 48 features for Wyoming, measured 2026-11-12. The unified districts and the elementary districts together cover the state's land (251,242 and 216 km2 of Wyoming's 251,458 km2), and TIGERweb's secondary layer carries nothing for Wyoming, so it is not drawn. One unified record is not a district: the Census files ground no school district reaches as "School District Not Defined" (GEOID 5699997). The Census files about 4,499 km2 of LAND, all in Park County, under the placeholder: Canyon Village and Mammoth Hot Springs in Yellowstone National Park fall inside it, and Cody does not (measured 2026-11-12). So the unified count above is 47 real districts and the placeholder. The card says no school district is defined there.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap wy-school-board-members.
source.applies: Wyoming — statewide, with the elementary district.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 180 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Wyoming (233 in the app's bounding box), about 1,397 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Wyoming (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='56'. The app's box reaches into Montana, South Dakota, Nebraska, Colorado, Utah and Idaho, and measured 2026-11-12, 180 of the 233 ZCTAs in it reach into Wyoming and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Wyoming. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 99 incorporated cities and towns, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or town containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 99 records: 80 towns and 19 cities, every one an active government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF WYOMING IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY OR TOWN (under 1% of its land, 921.9 of 251,458.2 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Wyoming's local officials was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap wy-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Wyoming has 2 pieces, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-11-13, with the counties measured against this app's own county outlines: the Wind River Reservation (9,128.7 km², Fremont and Hot Springs counties) and its trust land (20.4 km², Hot Springs County), both held by the Eastern Shoshone Tribe and the Northern Arapaho Tribe together. The Census draws no tribal district on either. Ranked after municipalities and before the point layers, as Nevada's and Arizona's are, so they are drawn above the larger areas around them. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on the Wind River Reservation or its trust land, and that the Eastern Shoshone Tribe and the Northern Arapaho Tribe, which share it, answer for it.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: No council is named yet. Each nation publishes its own council, and this app has not yet read those pages, so every card says so and links the nation's own site where there is one (ROSTER_NOT_SOUGHT in scripts/build_tribal_areas.py); the councils are to be read and carried one nation at a time. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json), which lists the Eastern Shoshone Tribe and the Northern Arapaho Tribe separately; they share the Wind River Reservation, so each card names both with their seats and sites. The land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Wyoming — the Wind River Reservation and its trust land, in Fremont and Hot Springs counties. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 81 points in Wyoming's envelope, which reaches into Montana, South Dakota, Nebraska, Colorado, Utah and Idaho; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Wyoming — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Wyoming State Capitol, 200 West 24th Street, Cheyenne, Laramie County

negative_point.note: Larimer County, Colorado, south of the Wyoming line — outside Wyoming and inside permalink_gate, so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names Colorado here (control: the Wyoming State Capitol returns Wyoming), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and of every outline in the fleet only Colorado's does (Colorado went live in batch 3 of the state-level launch). Wyoming borders no water and no other country, and every one of its neighbours (Montana, South Dakota, Nebraska, Colorado, Utah and Idaho) is live once this change lands, so no point this app's gate reaches lies outside every instance: the point stays where it is, as Illinois's sits in Indiana's waters, and a selection the app makes from its own link never leaves for another app.

geometry.note: The whole-Wyoming outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (23 counties).
Wyoming's 23 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The one U.S. House district, the whole state ("Congressional District (at Large)"), TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same as layer 4 (CD119).
The 31 Wyoming Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 62 Wyoming House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Wyoming's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — the Wind River Reservation and its off-reservation trust land, at the Census's own detail (216 KB). The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-11-13; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Wyoming elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from wy/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
